target.title: fix(slack): keep inbound message preview truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
<!--
AI-assisted: generated with Cursor / Claude Sonnet 4.6
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Slack messages containing emoji near the 160-character boundary produce an invalid `preview` string in the `PreparedSlackMessage` shape returned by `prepareSlackMessage`.

When an inbound Slack message is prepared for dispatch, a 160-character preview is built from the raw message body by collapsing whitespace and calling `.slice(0, 160)`. Emoji and supplementary-plane characters use two UTF-16 code units (a surrogate pair). A cut that lands between the two halves of a surrogate pair produces a lone high surrogate — invalid Unicode — in the `preview` field that is stored on the `PreparedSlackMessage` object and passed to the dispatch pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `.slice(0, 160)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 160)`, which detects and avoids splitting surrogate pairs. The preceding `.replace(/\s+/g, " ")` is unchanged. `truncateUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` is the established helper for this class of fix throughout the codebase.

## User Impact

Long Slack messages containing emoji that straddle the 160-character preview boundary produce a `PreparedSlackMessage` with an invalid `preview` string. Any consumer of that field — system event labels, monitoring, or debug output — receives malformed Unicode. After this fix the `preview` field is always a valid Unicode string regardless of message content.

## Evidence

- **`prepare.ts:1169`** (pre-fix): `const preview = rawBody.replace(/\s+/g, " ").slice(0, 160);`
- `preview` is a named field in `PreparedSlackMessage` (typed in `types.ts:38`) and returned from the function, so it flows into whatever the dispatch layer uses it for.
- **Fix:** `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 160)` — same cap, surrogate-safe.
- **Diff:** 2-line change — one new import, one call-site replacement; no logic change.
- `truncateUtf16Safe` is already imported in the sibling file `approval-handler.runtime.ts` in the same Slack extension, confirming the import path is correct.
